authors: Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology

papers.title: Hierarchical Planning for Long-Horizon Autonomous Agents
papers.abstract: We study decision-making agents that must complete tasks spanning thousands of primitive actions. We propose a hierarchical planner that decomposes goals into reusable sub-policies learned via offline demonstrations, and show that it reduces planning time by an order of magnitude on household-robotics and logistics benchmarks compared to flat search-based planners.

papers.title: A Framework for Explainable Multi-Agent Coordination
papers.abstract: Multi-agent systems increasingly coordinate in high-stakes settings such as traffic control and supply chains. We introduce a coordination framework that produces natural-language justifications for each agent's action alongside a formal audit trail, and evaluate it on simulated fleet-management scenarios where explanation quality is judged by human raters.

papers.title: Sample-Efficient Meta-Learning via Task Embedding Reuse
papers.abstract: Few-shot learning methods often require large meta-training sets to generalize. We propose a task-embedding cache that reuses gradient information across structurally similar tasks, cutting meta-training sample requirements roughly in half on standard few-shot classification and regression benchmarks while matching baseline accuracy.

papers.title: Robust Gradient Boosting Under Label Noise
papers.abstract: Gradient boosted trees are widely used on tabular data but degrade sharply when training labels are noisy. We propose a reweighting scheme based on out-of-fold residual consistency and show consistent accuracy gains over standard XGBoost and LightGBM baselines across eleven noisy tabular datasets.

papers.title: Efficient Attention via Learned Sparsity Patterns
papers.abstract: Transformer self-attention scales quadratically with sequence length. We introduce a lightweight gating module that learns per-head sparsity masks during training, achieving near full-attention accuracy on long-document classification while reducing FLOPs by up to 60% at inference time.

papers.title: Curriculum Pretraining for Low-Resource Vision Transformers
papers.abstract: Vision transformers typically need large labelled corpora to outperform convolutional networks. We present a curriculum pretraining strategy that orders unlabeled images by estimated visual complexity, improving downstream fine-tuning accuracy on small-scale datasets by several percentage points relative to random-order pretraining.

papers.title: Weakly Supervised Segmentation for Medical Image Analysis
papers.abstract: Pixel-level medical image annotations are expensive to obtain. We propose a weakly supervised segmentation model trained only on image-level diagnostic labels, using class-activation refinement and anatomical priors, and evaluate it on chest X-ray and dermoscopy datasets against fully supervised baselines.

papers.title: Cross-Domain Object Detection for Autonomous Driving in Adverse Weather
papers.abstract: Object detectors trained on clear-weather driving data degrade in fog, rain, and snow. We introduce a domain-adaptation pipeline that synthesizes adverse-weather training examples and aligns feature statistics across domains, improving detection mAP substantially on real adverse-weather driving benchmarks.

papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented Summarization for Long Scientific Documents
papers.abstract: Abstractive summarizers struggle with documents exceeding standard transformer context windows. We combine a dense retriever over document sections with a constrained generation module, producing summaries of long scientific papers that are judged more faithful and complete than sliding-window baselines in human evaluation.

papers.title: Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning for Clinical Text De-identification
papers.abstract: Clinical notes contain sensitive patient information that must be removed before research use. We present a de-identification model trained with differential-privacy guarantees that maintains high recall on protected health information categories while limiting memorization of individual patient records.

papers.title: Detecting Adversarial Examples via Activation Consistency Checks
papers.abstract: Adversarial perturbations can fool image classifiers while remaining imperceptible to humans. We propose a detection method that flags inputs whose intermediate activations are inconsistent across lightly augmented copies, achieving high detection rates against several gradient-based and black-box attacks.

papers.title: A Longitudinal Study of Phishing Campaign Infrastructure Reuse
papers.abstract: We analyze eighteen months of phishing takedown data to measure how often attackers reuse hosting infrastructure across campaigns. Our findings show substantial infrastructure clustering, which we use to build an early-warning system that flags newly registered domains likely to host phishing content.

papers.title: Adaptive Indexing for Mixed Read-Write Workloads
papers.abstract: Static index structures are often mistuned for workloads that shift between read-heavy and write-heavy phases. We propose an adaptive index that monitors query patterns and incrementally restructures itself, improving throughput on mixed OLTP workloads relative to fixed B-tree and LSM-tree baselines.

papers.title: Approximate Query Processing with Learned Cardinality Estimators
papers.abstract: Cardinality estimation errors are a major source of poor query plans. We train a lightweight neural estimator on query-execution feedback and integrate it into a PostgreSQL-compatible planner, reducing estimation error and end-to-end query latency on standard OLAP benchmarks.

papers.title: Fault-Tolerant Consensus for Geo-Distributed Edge Clusters
papers.abstract: Edge computing deployments span unreliable wide-area links. We adapt a leaderless consensus protocol to tolerate high-latency, lossy links between edge clusters, demonstrating lower tail latency than Raft-based baselines under simulated network partitions.

papers.title: Elastic Resource Scheduling for Stream Processing Pipelines
papers.abstract: Streaming workloads exhibit bursty, unpredictable load. We present a scheduler that predicts short-term load spikes from recent throughput history and proactively rebalances operators across a cluster, reducing backpressure events compared to reactive autoscaling baselines.

papers.title: Cost-Aware Serverless Function Placement Across Multi-Cloud Regions
papers.abstract: Serverless platforms rarely optimize jointly for cost and latency across cloud providers. We formulate function placement as a constrained optimization problem and propose a heuristic scheduler that reduces monthly compute cost while keeping p99 latency within service-level targets across three public cloud providers.

papers.title: Energy-Efficient Virtual Machine Consolidation in Data Centers
papers.abstract: Data center energy consumption is dominated by underutilized virtual machines. We propose a consolidation algorithm that migrates VMs based on predicted future load rather than instantaneous utilization, reducing active server count and associated energy use in trace-driven simulations.

papers.title: Interpretable Time-Series Anomaly Detection for Industrial IoT
papers.abstract: Anomaly detectors for industrial sensor data are often opaque black boxes. We propose a detection model built on interpretable change-point features that gives maintenance engineers human-readable explanations for flagged anomalies, evaluated on multi-sensor manufacturing datasets.

papers.title: Fairness-Aware Feature Selection for Credit Risk Models
papers.abstract: Feature selection choices can inadvertently encode demographic bias into credit-scoring models. We propose a feature-selection procedure that jointly optimizes predictive accuracy and a fairness-gap penalty, producing credit models with reduced disparate impact at a modest accuracy cost.

papers.title: Benchmarking Transfer Learning Across Low-Resource Languages
papers.abstract: Transfer learning has closed much of the performance gap for high-resource languages but low-resource languages remain underserved. We benchmark eight transfer strategies across eighteen low-resource languages and find that intermediate-language pivoting consistently outperforms direct fine-tuning on translation and classification tasks.

papers.title: Graph Neural Networks for Drug-Target Interaction Prediction
papers.abstract: Predicting whether a candidate molecule binds a target protein is central to drug discovery. We propose a graph neural network that jointly encodes molecular graphs and protein contact maps, improving interaction-prediction accuracy over fingerprint-based baselines on public bioactivity datasets.

papers.title: Federated Learning Under Non-IID Client Data Distributions
papers.abstract: Federated learning performance degrades when client data distributions differ substantially. We propose a client-clustering strategy that groups similar clients before aggregation, improving convergence speed and final accuracy on heterogeneous federated benchmarks relative to standard FedAvg.

papers.title: Self-Supervised Representation Learning for Satellite Imagery
papers.abstract: Labelled satellite imagery is scarce relative to the volume of raw sensor data collected. We propose a self-supervised pretraining objective tailored to multi-spectral satellite bands, improving downstream land-cover classification accuracy with a fraction of the labelled data required by supervised baselines.

papers.title: A Query Optimizer Extension for Vector Similarity Joins
papers.abstract: Modern applications increasingly combine relational filters with nearest-neighbour vector search. We extend a cost-based query optimizer to reason jointly about selectivity of relational predicates and approximate vector search, producing query plans that outperform naive filter-then-search pipelines.

papers.title: Byzantine-Resilient Federated Aggregation for Healthcare Networks
papers.abstract: Federated learning across hospitals is vulnerable to malicious or faulty participants. We propose a robust aggregation rule that down-weights updates inconsistent with a trusted validation set, maintaining model accuracy under a substantial fraction of Byzantine clients in simulated hospital networks.

papers.title: Serverless Cold-Start Mitigation via Predictive Pre-Warming
papers.abstract: Cold starts remain a major source of latency in serverless platforms. We propose a pre-warming policy that predicts near-future invocation bursts from historical traffic patterns, reducing cold-start rate substantially with modest additional idle-instance cost in trace-driven evaluation.

papers.title: Counterfactual Explanations for Tabular Deep Learning Models
papers.abstract: Deep tabular models are increasingly used in lending and hiring decisions where explainability matters. We propose a counterfactual-generation method constrained to produce actionable, realistic feature changes, and evaluate explanation plausibility against gradient-based and rule-based baselines with human raters.

papers.title: Scalable Approximate Nearest Neighbour Search on Billion-Scale Embeddings
papers.abstract: Recommendation and retrieval systems increasingly operate over billion-scale embedding collections. We combine product quantization with a learned routing layer to reduce memory footprint and query latency relative to standard IVF-PQ indexes on public billion-scale ANN benchmarks.

papers.title: Vision-Language Pretraining for Zero-Shot Document Classification
papers.abstract: Document images combine visual layout and textual content that single-modality models fail to exploit jointly. We pretrain a vision-language model on paired document image and OCR-text corpora, achieving strong zero-shot classification accuracy on unseen document categories.
